documents.prompt: Solve $x^2{{B|signed}}x{{C|signed}}=0$ by FACTORING. Write the complete solution set.

solutionReview.headline: Factoring turns one quadratic equation into two linear equations.
reasoning: Set each factor equal to zero to get $x={{r1}}$ and $x={{r2}}$.

attemptFeedback: Find two integers whose sum matches the middle coefficient and whose product matches the constant.
supportHints: After factoring, apply the zero-product property to both factors.

documents.prompt: Solve $(x-({{h}}))^2={{sq}}$ using the SQUARE-ROOT PROPERTY. Write the complete solution set.

solutionReview.headline: Taking a square root creates two branches.
reasoning: Adding {{h}} gives the two solutions {{r1}} and {{r2}}.

attemptFeedback: Do not lose the positive/negative pair when taking the square root.

documents.prompt: Solve $x^2{{mid|signed}}x={{rhs}}$ by COMPLETING THE SQUARE. Write the complete solution set.

solutionReview.headline: Add the same square-completing value to both sides.
reasoning: Half of the $x$-coefficient is {{p}}, so add ${{psq}}$ to both sides and rewrite the left as $(x+{{p}})^2$.
The right side becomes {{tsq}}, so $x+{{p}}=\pm{{t}}$, giving {{r1}} and {{r2}}.

attemptFeedback: Take half the coefficient of $x$, square it, and add that value to BOTH sides.
supportHints: Your left side should become a perfect-square trinomial before you take square roots.

documents.prompt: Solve ${{A}}x^2{{B|signed}}x{{C|signed}}=0$ using the QUADRATIC FORMULA. Write the complete solution set.

solutionReview.headline: Substitute $a$, $b$, and $c$ into the quadratic formula without dropping either sign.
reasoning: Evaluating $(-b\pm\sqrt{b^2-4ac})/(2a)$ simplifies to the two roots {{r1}} and {{r2}}.

attemptFeedback: Identify $a$, $b$, and $c$ with their signs before substituting.
supportHints: The $\pm$ creates two solutions; calculate both.

documents.prompt: A student solves $(x-({{h}}))^2={{sq}}$ and writes only $x={{r2}}$. Correct the student's work by writing the COMPLETE solution set.

solutionReview.headline: The student kept only the positive square-root branch.
reasoning: Taking square roots gives $x-({{h}})=\pm{{s}}$, not only $+{{s}}$.
The negative branch gives {{r1}} and the positive branch gives {{r2}}.

attemptFeedback: Find the branch the student omitted when taking the square root.
supportHints: A positive squared value usually has two real square roots.
